answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable stake of work. Imagine a wharf where every ship must pay a mooring fee before docking: agents lock a deposit that is slashed if they misbehave, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a raven learning the layout of a terrace over many visits. New agents start with limited trust and earn more only through sustained honest trades, so attackers face real cost while honest agents face only patience.
